# Using Tools Through Frontend Chat Interface

## Example Conversation Flow

**User**: "Read the file example-data.txt and insert all client data into the database"

**AI Assistant**: 
"Okay, I'll help you with that. First, let me read the file example-data.txt to see what data we have."

**Tool Call Generated by AI**:
```
{
  "toolName": "read_file",
  "arguments": "{\"path\":\"example-data.txt\"}"
}
```

**After File Reading Result**:
"File content retrieved successfully. I can see 3 clients in the file."

**AI Assistant**: 
"Now I'll create each client in the database using the ore-tracking API."

**Tool Calls Generated by AI**:
```
{
  "toolName": "ore_create_client",
  "arguments": "{\"name\":\"Acme Corp\",\"email\":\"contact@acme.com\",\"phone\":\"+1-555-0123\"}"
}

{
  "toolName": "ore_create_client",
  "arguments": "{\"name\":\"Beta Ltd\",\"email\":\"info@beta.com\",\"phone\":\"+1-555-0456\"}"
}

{
  "toolName": "ore_create_client",
  "arguments": "{\"name\":\"Gamma Inc\",\"email\":\"support@gamma.com\",\"phone\":\"+1-555-0789\"}"
}
```

## Manual Tool Execution

You can also manually execute tools from the chat interface:

1. Click on the "Tools" button (🛠️ Tools) to open the tools panel
2. Select a tool like "ore_create_client" 
3. The system will generate a tool call with default arguments
4. Modify the arguments as needed and click "Execute"

## Frontend Tool Display

In the chat interface, when tools are called:
- Tool calls appear below the AI response
- Each tool shows its name and arguments
- You can execute tools manually by clicking "Execute"
- Results are displayed below each tool call

## Example Manual Execution

**User**: "Create a new client named 'Delta Corp' with email 'info@delta.com'"

**Tool Call Generated**:
```
{
  "toolName": "ore_create_client",
  "arguments": "{\"name\":\"Delta Corp\",\"email\":\"info@delta.com\",\"phone\":\"\"}"
}
```

This demonstrates how the frontend chat interface allows both automatic tool execution by the AI and manual tool invocation by the user.
